'''James Bruce Walsh''' (born 1957)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n97055329.html |title=Walsh, Bruce, 1957– |website=Library of Congress Name Authority File |access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref> is an American geneticist whose research focuses on [[evolutionary genetics|evolutionary]] and [[quantitative genetics]]. He has been Professor of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology at the [[University of Arizona]] since 1986.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://eeb.arizona.edu/person/j-bruce-walsh |title=J. Bruce Walsh |date=2019-12-03 |website=University of Arizona |language=en |access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref> He discovered the [[moth]] species ''[[Lithophane leeae]]'' in 2009,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Walsh |first=J. |date=2009-05-12 |title=Lithophane leeae (Lepidoptera, Noctuidae, Xyleninae), a striking new species from southeastern Arizona |url=https://zookeys.pensoft.net/articles.php?id=1983 |journal=ZooKeys |issue=9 |pages=21–26 |doi=10.3897/zookeys.9.184 |bibcode=2009ZooK....9...21W |issn=1313-2970|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Arizona |first=Bruce Walsh / University of |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna31206672 |title=Pink moth discovered in Arizona |date=2009-06-10 |work=NBC News |access-date=2020-04-28 |language=en}}</ref> and another moth species, ''[[Drasteria walshi]]'', is named after him.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bugguide.net/node/view/785592 |title=Species Drasteria walshi |website=bugguide.net |access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref>
